title: The Intelligent Investor
author: Benjamin Graham
blurb: First published in 1949 and revised several times, The Intelligent Investor is Benjamin Graham's guide to investing sensibly without needing genius or luck. Graham draws a firm line between investing, which rests on careful analysis and protecting your money, and speculating, which is betting on price moves. He argues that the biggest danger to most investors is not the market but their own emotions. Through his famous character Mr. Market, he shows how to treat wild price swings as opportunities rather than orders. He explains how to split money between stocks and bonds, how to choose an approach that matches the effort you can give, and how to judge a company as a real business. Everything rests on one principle: always buy with a margin of safety.

lessons.b: Graham defines investing as an operation that, after careful analysis, promises safety of your money and a fair return, and anything else is speculation.

lessons.t: Meet Your Moody Partner, Mr. Market
lessons.b: The market is like an emotional business partner who offers you a different price every day, and you should take advantage of his moods rather than be ruled by them.
